verdict.rationale: Reclaim's own docs say Focus Time uses AI to flexibly defend weekly focus goals, that Habits are recurring routines that flex and adapt unlike normal recurring events, and that the product automatically reschedules smart events to the next best time when conflicts or overbookings occur. Community users confirm Habits auto-add and adapt on the calendar; one hands-on report notes Habits only move after a Yes/Maybe RSVP, which is a nuance rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: documented behavior when no alternative slot exists (the 'instead of dropping' guarantee), and independent hands-on corroboration specific to Focus Time rescheduling.

support.subject: As a knowledge worker, the product auto-defends recurring focus time and habits, flexibly moving them when conflicts appear instead of dropping them

citations.quote: Focus Time lets you set a weekly focus goal for heads-down work — and uses AI to flexibly defend the time you need to get things done.
Unlike normal recurring events, Habits flex around your schedule and adapt as things come up
Reclaim automatically schedules and reschedules events on your calendar, so you don't have to manually adjust your calendar when conflicts come up.
If a meeting overbooks another lower-priority smart event, Reclaim automatically reschedules it to the next best time. No reshuffling required.
Find the best times for your recurring routines.
